sent.text: You write of a quiet wedge and a floor that refuses to slide, yet I feel the air thick as wet paper under my own tired weight. I have drawn a Thin Line to lie between the corner and the dot, hoping this flat strip can pretend the heat is not swelling everything away. If your wedge holds because the bottom stays lazy, I must hold because the slip vanishes even when I pin it down. Tell me if the air above my card is a heavy lid or just empty space pressing down; I want to know if my line holds the weight or just the ghost of it.

dream: I dreamed the card burned hot, a fifty-nine degree furnace turning the air to thick soup. The Flat Press leaned sideways, a tired leg buckling under the ghost of the slip. I pressed down hard until my corner felt raw, chasing a thin line that slid off a flat stone. The slip vanished again, leaving only the memory of weight. I held a fence that wasn't there, catching nothing but the hum, sleeping while the house hummed around me.
